key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the suicide note and FIR but found them suspicious and lacking in material for prosecution under Sections 306 and 294(b) of the IPC.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (the complainant and the deceased) as unreliable, noting the suspicious origin of the suicide note and the lack of credible evidence linking the accused to the deceased's suicide.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 15.10.2007 to 23.2.2008; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: Dismissed the petition under Section 482 CrPC; Supreme Court decision: Allowed the appeal and quashed the FIR and further proceedings
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: K.T.S. Tulsi, Priyanka Agarwal, Niraj Gupta, Hemantika Wahi, Nachiketa Joshi (for Minakshi Vij); Counsel for the State: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR registered (C.R. No. 166 of 2008 at Naranpura Police Station), suicide note alleged, FIR and further proceedings quashed by Supreme Court
appeal_history: Trial court: Not stated; High Court: Dismissed the petition under Section 482 CrPC; Supreme Court: Allowed the appeal and quashed the FIR and further proceedings
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the FIR and the suicide note indicated that the appellant had harassed the deceased, leading to his suicide, and thus constituted offences under Sections 306 and 294(b) of the IPC.
defence_argument: The appellant contended that even if the suicide note and FIR were accepted, they did not contain the necessary ingredients to establish an offence under Sections 306 and 294(b) IPC, as there was no specific abetment or intention to cause the deceased's suicide.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle that for an offence under Section 306 IPC, there must be specific abetment as contemplated by Section 107 IPC, with an intention to bring about the suicide of the deceased.
precedent_relied_upon: Netai Dutta v. State of WB. 2005 (2) SCC 659; State of Haryana & Ors. v. Bhajan Lal & Ors. 1992 Suppl. 1 SCC 335
